headline: ASX closes up 0.38% while oil takes a dramatic 5% tumble, and the RBA signals rates are heading higher to cool the jobs market.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced nicely today, up 1.2% to $4.18, riding a broader ASX recovery and some positive sentiment around the long-term lithium battery market outlook. A new market forecast projects 18–22% annual growth in grid storage lithium demand through to 2035 — good for the long-term thesis, even if the near-term lithium price remains soft.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI edged up 0.53% today as AI sector sentiment stayed positive — there's a lot of news flow around new model launches from OpenAI and Anthropic (more in the AI section). The position is still down about 8.8% overall, but today's move is a small step in the right direction.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS ticked up 0.3% today to $537.36, continuing its steady climb — it's now up 4.2% on your total investment. This ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket, so it reflects last night's Wall Street performance priced in AUD. No major news driving this beyond broad market stability.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG crept up 0.13% today — a quiet session for this diversified fund, which holds a mix of Aussie and global shares. No specific news catalyst; just a gentle lift with the broader ASX. It's essentially flat on your total investment, which is fine for a long-term hold.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped a tiny 0.13% today to $94.67. Emerging markets can be sensitive to a stronger US dollar and global risk sentiment — neither of which was particularly helpful today. The AUD also weakened slightly. A negligible move; you're basically breakeven on this position overall.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: No updated price data for GOOG tonight — US markets haven't opened yet. Last close was $350.87 USD. Nothing specific in the news around Google today beyond the ongoing AI regulatory drumbeat in the UK parliament.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: No updated price data for MSFT tonight — US markets open later. Last session MSFT rose about 1.6% as investors look ahead to Q1 revenue results. Microsoft's AI push continues to be a key theme supporting its share price.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: No updated US price for TTWO tonight. Last close was $209.92 USD. There's some GTA 6 news flow — Take-Two's CEO signalled PC players should have hope for a PC release eventually, but no date confirmed. Rockstar is also actively removing leaked GTA 6 map assets. The long-term case here still rests on GTA 6 being one of the biggest game launches in history.

watch_today.title: RBA signals rate rise coming — mortgage stress ahead
watch_today.detail: The RBA Governor has explicitly said the heat needs to come out of the jobs market, and CBA and ANZ have both changed their rate call — now expecting a hike. This hits anyone with a variable mortgage. For your portfolio, rising rates are a headwind for growth stocks and can weigh on the ASX broadly. Worth watching this week for timing.

watch_today.title: Oil crashes 5% — big move with wide ripple effects
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped $4.78 to $89.81 today — a sharp 5% fall. That's good for inflation (cheaper petrol, cheaper transport costs), which could actually take some pressure off the RBA. But it also weighs on energy stocks globally. Nothing in your direct portfolio is oil-exposed, but it's a significant macro signal.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — hold, but the picture is slowly improving
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals bounced 1.2% today and new industry forecasts point to strong long-term lithium demand growth (18–22% CAGR to 2035 for grid storage). You're still down about 38% on this position, which stings — but the long-term thesis around battery metals and the energy transition hasn't changed. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — hold, AI sector momentum building
watch_today.detail: GXAI was up 0.53% today and there's serious AI news flow: OpenAI launched GPT-6, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, and both companies are rolling out cheaper models. That's good for the AI sector broadly. You're down ~8.8% on this position but the underlying AI theme is as strong as ever. No reason to sell.

watch_today.title: TTWO — hold, GTA 6 story intact
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's CEO is actively hyping a PC version of GTA 6 and Rockstar is cracking down on leaks — both signs the game is still very much in focus. No date yet, but the long-term thesis (GTA 6 being a monster revenue event) remains intact. US markets open tonight — watch for any price movement.

watch_today.title: VTS.AX — hold, quiet strength continues
watch_today.detail: VTS is your best performer, up 4.2% on your investment and ticking up again today. It tracks the entire US market, so as long as the US economy holds up, this does its job. Nothing to do here — just let it compound.

world.summary: Trump rattled the UN General Assembly with an Iran ultimatum, oil tanked on Middle East deal hopes, the WEF warned of global economic risks, and Justin Trudeau resurfaced with a diplomatic lecture tour.

stories.title: Trump threatens to 'annihilate' Iran at UN — but expects a peace deal after November midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said the US could 'annihilate' Iran but that he fully expects a diplomatic deal to be struck — just not until after the November US midterm elections. Diplomats are quietly working on a framework. This is why oil dropped 5% today: markets are pricing in a possible easing of Middle East tension and a return of Iranian oil supply. If a deal happens, it would be a major geopolitical shift with global economic consequences — lower energy prices, reduced inflation pressure, and a de-escalation of the conflict that has rattled the region for months.

stories.title: WEF warns Middle East conflict is the biggest single threat to the global economy
stories.why_it_matters: The World Economic Forum's chief economists have released their latest global outlook, flagging that the Middle East conflict remains the single biggest threat to global economic stability. While the overall outlook is improving — with India cited as one of the strongest growth stories — uncertainty persists. For everyday Aussies, the key risk is energy prices: a flare-up in the Middle East can push petrol prices up fast, adding to cost-of-living pressure at exactly the wrong time given the RBA is already considering rate hikes.

stories.title: Justin Trudeau speaks at Brown University on US-Canada relations and global conflict
stories.why_it_matters: Former Canadian PM Justin Trudeau has resurfaced on the US university lecture circuit, speaking at Brown University about the strained US-Canada relationship under Trump, the nature of global conflict, and the importance of multilateral diplomacy. While Trudeau is no longer in office, his perspective reflects wider anxieties among US allies — including Australia — about the reliability of the US as a partner. The US-Canada trade relationship deteriorated sharply under Trump tariffs, and many of the same pressures are playing out in Australia's trade diplomacy.

stories.title: China watching Iran war closely — and playing both sides in the Middle East
stories.why_it_matters: A detailed analysis from the Arab Center Washington DC examines how China has been carefully positioning itself in the Middle East conflict — maintaining economic ties with Iran while avoiding direct military involvement, and quietly expanding influence with Gulf Arab states. China is Iran's biggest oil customer, so any US-Iran deal directly affects Beijing's energy supply chains. This matters for Australia because China is our biggest trading partner — anything that shifts China's economic stability or energy costs flows through to demand for Australian resources like iron ore and lithium.

stories.title: Korean and Australian leaders meet to discuss energy supply chains amid Middle East tensions
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's PM and South Korea's President met to discuss securing stable energy supply chains in the wake of Middle East conflict disruption. Both nations are heavily dependent on Middle East energy imports and are keen to diversify. For Australia, this is part of a broader push to deepen the economic relationship with Asia-Pacific neighbours — and potentially to position Australian LNG (liquefied natural gas) as a reliable alternative energy source for the region.

politics.summary: The RBA is all but certain to raise interest rates, with CBA and ANZ both updating their forecasts. Meanwhile, Australia and the US are clashing over an 'opt-out algorithm' law, and Albanese is being pressured to push back on Trump's interference.

stories.title: RBA governor signals rates are going up — CBA and ANZ change their calls
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Governor Michele Bullock has explicitly said 'heat' needs to be taken out of Australia's jobs market — central bank language that strongly signals a rate hike is coming. CBA and ANZ have now updated their forecasts to price in a rise. The AFR reports the RBA's inflation fight is likely to push unemployment higher as a side effect. For anyone with a variable-rate mortgage, this is a direct cost increase coming. For share investors, higher rates generally weigh on growth stocks and property values — worth factoring into your thinking.

stories.title: US attacks Australia's 'opt-out algorithm' law in rare diplomatic intervention
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has taken the unusual step of publicly criticising Australia's proposed algorithm law, which would let users 'opt out' of social media recommendation algorithms. Washington argues the law unfairly targets US tech companies. It puts PM Albanese in an awkward spot — caught between protecting Australians from algorithmic harm and not upsetting the Trump administration at a delicate time in the bilateral relationship. Opposition figures and some commentators are urging Albanese to stand firm and reject what they're calling US interference in domestic law-making.

stories.title: Former treasurer says Australia needs a 'financial crisis' to push through economic reform
stories.why_it_matters: A former Australian Treasurer has made the blunt observation that Australia's political system seems incapable of delivering serious structural economic reform — tax, superannuation, housing — without a genuine crisis forcing the issue. With the RBA about to hike rates and cost-of-living pressure at a multi-decade high, the question of whether the government has the political will to reform (rather than just manage) is front of mind for economists and voters alike.

ai.summary: Massive AI news day: OpenAI launched GPT-6, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, both companies are being hauled before UK parliament over safety concerns, and there's a new antitrust lawsuit alleging the big AI players secretly agreed to slow development.

stories.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 — two models called 'Sol' and 'Luna'
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI has officially released GPT-6, coming in two versions — 'Sol' and 'Luna'. This is the next major leap from GPT-4 and the o-series models. While detailed benchmarks aren't yet widely reported, GPT-6 represents OpenAI's flagship product in an increasingly competitive race with Anthropic and Google. This is directly relevant to your GXAI.AX holding — new, more powerful models drive demand for AI infrastructure and services, which is the engine that ETF is designed to capture.

stories.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5 — cheaper and more capable
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic has launched Claude Opus 5.5 — a more powerful and cheaper version of its flagship model. Both Anthropic and OpenAI are releasing cheaper models at the same time, following a public debate about whether AI development should slow down for safety reasons. The price cuts are significant: lower costs mean more businesses can integrate AI, accelerating adoption. This is the kind of trend that should benefit your GXAI.AX position over the medium term.

stories.title: UK Parliament summons Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic over AI safety fears
stories.why_it_matters: The UK Parliament's Business Committee has formally invited the bosses of Meta, Google, OpenAI and Anthropic to appear before a public hearing on AI safety. This is part of a growing global push for regulation — Australia has backed tougher AI rules, and Trump at the UN has rejected any regulation at all. The tension between 'move fast' and 'move safely' is the defining political battle in tech right now. More regulation could slow some AI revenue growth, but also legitimises AI as a mainstream industry.

stories.title: Antitrust lawsuit: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and SpaceX AI accused of secretly agreeing to slow AI development
stories.why_it_matters: A new antitrust lawsuit has been filed against OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and SpaceX's AI division, alleging they secretly agreed to coordinate on slowing AI development — effectively cartel-like behaviour in the AI race. If proven, this would be a massive legal and reputational blow to the industry's biggest players. It's early days and the legal bar is high, but it's the kind of case that could drag on for years and create regulatory uncertainty. Worth monitoring for your GXAI.AX holding.

sport.summary: NRL Finals Week 2 results are in — the Roosters pulled off a miracle win over the Raiders, and the Dolphins had a back suffer a suspension heading into their huge Friday night clash. AFL Grand Final week is here, and the North Melbourne coaching search is getting complicated.

stories.title: Roosters stun Raiders in Finals Week 2 — miracle comeback after halftime speech
stories.why_it_matters: The Roosters have made it through to Finals Week 3 after a dramatic come-from-behind win over the Raiders. Fox Sports reports words spoken at halftime sparked the turnaround — the Roosters are now set to play the Dolphins at Suncorp on Friday night at 7:50pm. Meanwhile, a Dolphins back has been hit with a suspension, which is a significant blow to their preparation for that clash. The Raiders' season is over.

stories.title: Titans knocked out — Broncos advance in Finals Week 2
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans have been knocked out of the 2026 finals after losing to the Brisbane Broncos in Finals Week 2. The Broncos advance to Week 3. Hard to take for local Gold Coast fans — the Titans' season is done.

stories.title: Warriors centre released mid-finals — likely suitor emerges
stories.why_it_matters: A New Zealand Warriors centre has been released by the club mid-finals, with CODE Sports reporting a likely suitor has already emerged. The NRL player market is moving fast even as the finals are being played — clubs are positioning for 2027 rosters.

stories.title: AFL Grand Final week: Ultimate guide, plus another coach pulls out of North Melbourne race
stories.why_it_matters: AFL Grand Final week is here and The Australian has published a full guide. Separately, another premiership-winning coach has withdrawn from the race to become North Melbourne's new senior coach, further complicating the Kangaroos' search. The AFL trade period is also about to kick off, with Trade Radio returning to AFL.com.au.
